newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil due to announce federal cost-cutting plan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil due to announce federal cost-cutting plan.

text.p: Brazil's finance, planning, federal administration and social security ministers were due to announce at 1330 local/1530 GMT a federal cost-cutting plan, a Finance Ministry spokeswoman said.

Newspapers reported that the plan, including a slashing of privileges for public sector servants, a voluntary redundancy scheme and measures to raise social security contributions, could save 1.4 billion reais.
The package was first announced by Brazilian ministers in the United States, who said then it could involve the sale or liquidation of up to 24 state firms and save 2.5 billion reais.

Concern over the fiscal accounts has gradually spread in government circles after the operational deficit reached 3.72 percent of gross domestic product in the first seven months compared with a target of 2.5-2.9 percent for the year.
The plan is intended to show Brazil can improve its fiscal situation without necessarily depending on the swift passage of fiscal reforms through a recalcitrant Congress, officials say.
